summary: Hong Kong is now DR-verified. Keeping a pet roof rat is legal, Rattus rattus is not protected wildlife (the family Muridae is omitted from Schedule 2 of the Wild Animals Protection Ordinance, Cap. 170), so no possession licence is needed, but it sits under a public-health overlay: the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department treats all rodents as 'vermin' under Cap. 132 with no carve-out for kept pets, enforced on a complaint/infestation basis rather than against sanitarily-caged pets. Private breeding is unregulated (Hong Kong licenses only dog breeders); selling 'by way of business' needs an Animal Trader Licence, though a hobbyist exemption covers selling a pet's offspring and giving one away free is unregulated. Importing any mammal needs an AFCD Special Permit + government-vet health certificate + rabies quarantine (the 2022 COVID small-mammal import ban was lifted by Jan 2023).

keep.why: Rattus rattus is not a protected wild animal, the family Muridae is omitted from Schedule 2 of the Wild Animals Protection Ordinance (Cap. 170), so no possession licence is required. Caveat: the Public Health and Municipal Services Ordinance (Cap. 132, s.47) defines all rodents as 'vermin' with no carve-out for caged pets, a public-health overlay the FEHD enforces on a complaint/infestation basis (elimination notices, not raids on kept pets).
keep.governing_law: Cap. 170 Sch. 2 (wildlife, Muridae omitted); Cap. 132 s.47 (FEHD 'vermin' duty).

breed.why: Private, non-commercial breeding is unregulated: Hong Kong created dedicated breeder licences only for dogs (Cap. 139B), deliberately leaving small mammals unregulated at the breeding stage. Oversight begins only at the point of commercial sale.
breed.governing_law: Cap. 139B (dog breeder licences only; small mammals unregulated at breeding).

sell_give.why: Selling 'by way of business' requires an Animal Trader Licence (Cap. 139B s.4), but a statutory HOBBYIST EXEMPTION covers selling an animal 'kept by him as a pet or any offspring thereof', and giving one away free (no consideration) is unregulated. Note: the ATL's permitted 'domestic rats' is widely read as the fancy R. norvegicus, so commercial sale of R. rattus is legally untested.
sell_give.governing_law: Cap. 139B s.4 (Animal Trader Licence + pet/offspring hobbyist exemption).

transport.why: Internal movement of a lawfully-kept pet is unencumbered (subject only to anti-cruelty Cap. 169). IMPORT of any live mammal requires an AFCD Special Permit (Form AF240 commercial / AF242a personal) plus a government-vet Veterinary Health Certificate, with rabies quarantine set by the export country's risk group (Cap. 139; Cap. 421). The 2022 COVID small-mammal import ban was fully lifted by Jan 2023.
transport.governing_law: Cap. 139 s.5 + Cap. 421 (import Special Permit + vet health cert + rabies quarantine); Cap. 169 (humane transport).

restrictions.summary: Keeping a captive-bred roof rat is allowed in Hong Kong; selling needs an AFCD Animal Trader Licence, and importing needs an AFCD Special Permit (AF240) + health certificate, note AFCD has SUSPENDED commercial/unaccompanied rodent imports (owner-accompanied may still be approved). Keep proof your rat is captive-bred (re: the Cap. 132 'vermin' duty). Never release.
steps: For import: apply for an AFCD Special Permit (Form AF240) in advance + origin health certificate
For sale: obtain an Animal Trader Licence
restrictions.fees: Import permit HK$432 first animal + HK$102 each additional

inquiry_focus: (1) Does AFCD's suspension of commercial (unaccompanied) rodent imports apply equally to a private hobbyist importing one or two personally-accompanied captive-bred Rattus rattus as pets, or can a Special Permit (Form AF240) still issue for non-commercial personal rodent import? (2) Does AFCD or any HK authority interpret s.47 of Cap. 132 (the vermin-elimination duty) as applying to lawfully-kept captive-bred pet rats in a private dwelling, or only to feral/commensal infestation? (3) What is AFCD's position on the threshold between 'private breeding' (no ATL) and 'trading/breeding by way of business' under Cap. 139B for a hobbyist who rehomes occasional litters at no charge?
